transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what finally made me agree to come in is that I just don't care about the things that used to keep me balanced anymore. Like sailing races, or my Saturday shift at the historical society... even just tinkering out in the woodshop. They all just feel like chores now, and I just keep putting them off.
Have you noticed that you no longer enjoy activities that used to make you happy, like sailing races or working in the woodshop?

Yeah, exactly what I was just saying. I just don't care about them anymore. The sailing, the woodshop, even my shift at the historical society... they used to keep me balanced, but now I don't get any enjoyment out of them at all. They just feel like chores that I keep putting off.
Do you find yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
No, I wouldn't say I feel down or depressed most of the time. It's more just... a lack of interest, I guess. I don't really feel sad or anything like that on a daily basis.
Have you been experiencing a lack of energy or feeling fatigued lately, even when you haven't done much physically or mentally?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with my energy levels. I don't feel particularly tired or fatigued, just... like I said, I just don't have the drive to do my usual hobbies. But physically, my energy is fine.
How long have you been feeling this way about your hobbies and usual activities?
It's been going on since the scaffold accident... that was during the business readjustment. So, I guess it's been a little over a year now.
Have you noticed any other changes in how you feel, like trouble concentrating, feeling guilty, or thinking that you're not worth much?

Well, my concentration is fine, and I don't feel worthless or anything like that. But as for feeling guilty... yeah, I do have that. 

There's just this low-grade dread and guilt that kind of follows me around now. I keep thinking that I should have seen one more risk coming with that scaffold, you know? People keep telling me that all the proper controls were in place, but... I still just feel like I should have caught it.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things even when others have reassured you that you're not at fault?

Yeah, that's exactly what I mean. It's really just tied to that scaffold incident. Even with everyone telling me I did everything right and it wasn't my fault, I still blame myself for it. But I don't really go around feeling guilty about other things in my day-to-day life. It's pretty much just focused on that one specific event.
Do you find that this guilt about the scaffold incident affects how you see yourself overall, or do you feel it’s limited to thoughts about that specific event?

No, I wouldn't say it affects how I see myself overall. I mean... I know I'm competent. I've been doing project management for a long time, and I know I have a good track record. I don't walk around thinking I'm a failure or a bad person or anything like that. 

It really is just limited to that specific accident. It's just... that one day, that one event where I feel like I missed something. But outside of that, my overall view of myself hasn't really changed.
Can you describe how often this lack of interest in your usual activities occurs? Is it every day, most days, or more occasional?

It's most days. Honestly, that's what finally made me agree to come in and talk to someone. I just... I don't care about the things that used to keep me balanced. 

Things like sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, or even just tinkering out in the woodshop. They all just feel like chores now, and I keep putting them off. So yeah, it's a pretty constant feeling lately.
Have you ever felt guilty or blamed yourself for things outside of the scaffold incident, even when others told you it wasn’t your fault?

No, not really. Like I mentioned before, it's pretty much just that one incident with the scaffold. I don't really have a problem with feeling guilty or blaming myself for other things in my life. It's just that one specific event that I can't seem to shake.
Outside of the feelings related to the scaffold incident, do you ever feel a general sense of emptiness or sadness that lasts for most of the day, even when there’s no specific reason for it?

No, I don't think so. I wouldn't say I feel empty or sad most of the day. Like I said, I just don't have the energy or interest for my usual hobbies right now, but it's not really a general sadness. It's more just... feeling flat about those specific things. But I don't walk around feeling sad all day.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in other activities that you used to enjoy, outside of your hobbies like sailing or working at the historical society?

No, not really. It's pretty much just those main hobbies I mentioned. I still enjoy spending time with my family and, you know, watching a movie or something. It's just the bigger activities that I used to dedicate a lot of time to that I've lost interest in. The rest of my day-to-day stuff feels pretty normal.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past year, like eating more or less than usual or gaining or losing weight without trying?
No, my appetite has been pretty steady. I haven't noticed any weight gain or loss, really. I just eat my normal meals like I always have.
Do you find that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, not just your hobbies, even things you used to enjoy doing regularly?

No, not at all. Like I said before, it's really just the sailing and the historical society stuff that I don't care about right now. I still enjoy a lot of the regular things I do every day, so it's definitely not everything.
Do you experience a depressed mood, such as feeling sad, empty, or tearful, most of the day, nearly every day?
No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel sad or empty most of the time. My mood is generally fine day-to-day.
Do you find that you have little interest or pleasure in doing things, nearly every day?

No, not really. Like I mentioned, it's mostly just the sailing and the history group that I've lost interest in. I still get enjoyment out of my day-to-day routine, so it's not a constant thing where I don't care about anything.
Do you find that you have little interest or pleasure in doing things you used to enjoy, on most days?

Well, like I was saying, it's specific things. What finally made me agree to come in and talk to someone is that I just don't care about the things that used to keep me balanced. My sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, even tinkering out in the woodshop... they all just feel like chores now that I keep putting off. So it's those hobbies, mostly.
Do you feel a loss of interest or pleasure in almost all activities, even ones you used to enjoy, most of the time?

No, it's not almost all activities. Like I said, it's really just those specific hobbies I mentioned—the sailing, the historical society, the woodshop. I still enjoy my regular day-to-day stuff, so it's definitely not everything.
Outside of the scaffold incident, have you ever felt that you are not worth much or have blamed yourself for things that weren’t really your fault?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't really walk around feeling worthless or beating myself up over things that aren't my fault. I generally feel pretty okay about who I am and the work I do.
